data.content_ref: inline:{"analogy":null,"claim":"Resumption is categorically unsafe if and only if the append-only medium does not support atomic delimitation of events\u2014i.e., if a single write operation can produce a byte sequence that is indistinguishable from a complete event. When the medium supports atomic per-event writes (all-or-nothing delivery), every entry in the log is either a complete event or nothing, so token-budget exhaustion simply leaves the log at the last complete event, and resumption is always safe given a matching causal fingerprint.","counterconditions":[{"case":"If the medium supports atomic writes but the reasoning envelope buffers a partially-constructed event in memory and flushes it on exhaustion, the atomicity guarantee is circumvented.","eval":"observation"},{"case":"If atomic write granularity is larger than a single event (e.g., a page containing multiple events), a partial page write could corrupt multiple events.","eval":"observation"},{"case":"If the atomic-write guarantee is only eventual (e.g., fsync semantics), a crash before sync could leave a partial fragment despite the atomic-write API.","eval":"observation"}],"definitions":[],"derivation":[],"formalization_refs":[],"mechanism":"The root question is whether the write boundary is atomic. If the medium guarantees that each event is written atomically (either fully committed or not at all), then partial fragments are impossible by construction. Token-budget exhaustion interrupts the reasoning process between event emissions, not within one. The log contains zero or more complete events; resumption picks up at the next event. If the medium does not guarantee atomic writes, partial fragments are possible and the framing-quarantine protocol becomes necessary.","premises":[],"schema":"deepreason-reasoning-envelope-v1","scope":{"covers":[],"excludes":[]},"simulation_refs":[],"uncertainties":[]}
